item.title: Re: Document Leaks
item.content:encoded:
I've spent some of my free time in the last week or so creating some SCP documents in InDesign, and throughout the next week, I plan to leave them outside the staffrooms of relevant faculties in my school.

The documents I've done are:

  • SCP-049
  • SCP-701 (Including both sub-documents)
  • SCP-939 (Including all 3 sub-documents)
  • SCP-3477 (And it's one sub-document)
  • SCP-4645

Totalling to 11 different documents. Each of these is in a manilla folder. The photos, I printed on photo paper and paperclipped onto the documents.

049 and 939 are going to science teachers, 701 to english, 3477 to modern history and 4645 to a software teacher!

+ Images!
- I don't want to see the images anymore :(



I'll update this post as interesting developments occur!

Update: Nothing much of interest happened (oof).

item.title: Re: Document Leaks
item.content:encoded: Cool. Make sure you replace the "SCP-X" with a credible thing and attach the document, and make an extranormal event document as well as an anomalous object document that is related to the original scip. So if you used 173 for example, make the extranormal event "5 people were found in their homes with their necks snapped. No evidence of a struggle or suicide were found." and have the anomalous item a can of Krylon brand spray paint.

item.title: Re: Document Leaks
item.content:encoded:
I like it. Your included note seems a little awkward and odd though. I would put something more along the lines of:
"WARNING: THIS FILE CONTAINS CLASS C MEMETIC HAZARDS. NON-AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL AND CIVILIANS ARE ADVISED TO DISPOSE OF THIS FOLDER VIA INCINERATION.

Enclosed in file PFG-8193 are documents pertaining to local extranormal event 06-A and anomalous object 045. Possible connection to SCP-X is suspected. Attached is a picture of an instance of extranormal event 06-A and anomalous object 045."

Then print off a trippy/creepy/weird picture and attach it.

item.title: Re: Document Leaks
item.content:encoded:
So long as the files you include aren't likely to cause widespread paranoia (something something illegal to shout "fire!" in a crowded theater?) you should be fine.

Document drops are intended to inspire curiosity and interest for the site, not cause mass panic and potential emotional harm. Keep that in mind.

item.title: Re: Document Leaks
item.content:encoded:
"BURNED UNDER SUGGESTION OF THE SCP ETHICS COMMITTEE" sounds really silly to me. Generally it's "Foundation [department]", not "SCP" since that's just an acronym for the motto and procedures, it's not the actual organization.

Also, what kind of meta-document do you have in mind, and what are you going to do with it?

item.title: Re: Document Leaks
item.content:encoded:
I've been dropping off a few of my favorites here and there. I have these clear plastic envelopes that I put them in (big enough to hold the documents unfolded). I have a few SCPs done in Word format that I print up with a cover letter seemingly from one agent to another. The note is between people who obviously know each other, and is in a very familiar tone. The last bit is a warning "Not to lose these the way you did the last set", because Admin will be really pissed.

I have to be careful where I drop them. Several times I have had conscientious people notice I've left them behind and brought them out to me as I've left an establishment.

In a few cases I've added small vials with sand or gravel and a note stating it was considered anomalous and could he please drop it off at the lab in Site 19 the next time he's in the area?

I usually include a business card in the slot provided on the envelope, so they have a contact phone number.

Fun.
